Answer: B. The unusual vessel is positioned to the left of the aortic arch and drains into the left brachiocephalic vein, consistent with a vertical vein.  
Reason: In Figures 1b–1d, the white arrow identifies a vessel lying to the left of the aortic arch (Ao), coursing vertically between the left pulmonary artery and aorta, and connecting to the left brachiocephalic vein (as indicated by the star in Fig 1c/1d marking the confluence near the innominate vein); this matches the classic CT appearance of a vertical vein in partial anomalous pulmonary venous return with absent left upper pulmonary vein.
